sanskrit: nāhaṃ mithyāvaco brūyāṃ svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā bhavato yad ahaṃ brūyāṃ tat kāryam aviśaṅkayā
english: "I would not speak a false word even in jest, much less in a grave matter. Whatever I shall say to you must be carried out without any hesitation."

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca bravītu bhagavān mūlyaṃ maharṣeḥ sadṛśaṃ bhṛgoḥ paritrāyasva mām asmād viṣayaṃ ca kulaṃ ca me
english: Nahuṣa said: "Let the holy one name a price befitting the great sage, the son of Bhṛgu. Deliver me from this peril, and my kingdom, and my lineage."

sanskrit: hanyād dhi bhagavān kruddhas trailokyam api kevalam kiṃ punar māṃ tapohīnaṃ bāhuvīryaparāyaṇam
english: "For the holy one, when angered, could destroy even the entire threefold world—how much more easily me, who am devoid of austerity and rely only on the strength of my arms."

sanskrit: agādhe 'mbhasi magnasya sāmātyasya sahartvijaḥ plavo bhava maharṣe tvaṃ kuru mūlyaviniścayam
english: "To one sunk in fathomless waters, together with his ministers and his priests, be you a raft, O great sage. Determine the price."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nahuṣasya vacaḥ śrutvā gavijātaḥ pratāpavān uvāca harṣayan sarvān amātyān pārthivaṃ ca tam
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard the words of Nahuṣa, the majestic sage born of a cow spoke, gladdening all the ministers and that king as well.

sanskrit: anargheyā mahārāja dvijā varṇamahattamāḥ gāvaś ca pṛthivīpāla gaur mūlyaṃ parikalpyatām
english: "Beyond all price, O great king, are the twice-born, highest among the social orders, and so too are cows, O protector of the earth. Let a cow be reckoned as the price."

sanskrit: nahuṣas tu tataḥ śrutvā maharṣer vacanaṃ nṛpa harṣeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ sahāmātyapurohitaḥ
english: And then, O king, hearing the great sage's word, Nahuṣa was filled with great joy, together with his ministers and his household priest.

sanskrit: abhigamya bhṛgoḥ putraṃ cyavanaṃ saṃśitavratam idaṃ provāca nṛpate vācā saṃtarpayann iva
english: Approaching Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, firm in his vows, he spoke these words, O lord of men, as if soothing him with his speech.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha viprarṣe gavā krīto 'si bhārgava etan mūlyam ahaṃ manye tava dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: "Rise, rise, O sage among brahmins! With a cow you have been purchased, O scion of Bhṛgu. This I deem your price, O best of the upholders of dharma."

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca uttiṣṭhāmy eṣa rājendra samyak krīto 'smi te 'nagha gobhis tulyaṃ na paśyāmi dhanaṃ kiṃ cid ihācyuta
english: Cyavana said: "I rise, O lord of kings; rightly have I been bought by you, O sinless one. No wealth do I see in this world that is equal to cows, O unfailing one."

sanskrit: kīrtanaṃ śravaṇaṃ dānaṃ darśanaṃ cāpi pārthiva gavāṃ praśasyate vīra sarvapāpaharaṃ śivam
english: "To celebrate cows, to hear of them, to give them, and even to behold them, O king—all this is praised, O hero, as auspicious and the remover of every sin."

sanskrit: gāvo lakṣmyāḥ sadā mūlaṃ goṣu pāpmā na vidyate annam eva sadā gāvo devānāṃ paramaṃ haviḥ
english: "Cows are ever the root of prosperity; in cows no evil is found. Cows are always food itself, and the highest oblation of the gods."

sanskrit: svāhākāravaṣaṭkārau goṣu nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitau gāvo yajñapraṇetryo vai tathā yajñasya tā mukham
english: "The sacred utterances svāhā and vaṣaṭ are eternally established in cows. Cows are the very bearers of the sacrifice, and they are the mouth of the sacrifice."

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ hy akṣayaṃ divyaṃ kṣaranti ca vahanti ca amṛtāyatanaṃ caitāḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtāḥ
english: "They yield and they bear the nectar, imperishable and divine; they are the abode of immortality, revered by all the worlds."

sanskrit: tejasā vapuṣā caiva gāvo vahnisamā bhuvi gāvo hi sumahat tejaḥ prāṇināṃ ca sukhapradāḥ
english: "In radiance and in form, cows are like fire upon the earth; cows are a great splendor indeed, and bestowers of happiness upon living beings."

sanskrit: niviṣṭaṃ gokulaṃ yatra śvāsaṃ muñcati nirbhayam virājayati taṃ deśaṃ pāpmānaṃ cāpakarṣati
english: "Wherever a herd of cattle, settled and at ease, breathes freely without fear, it makes that land shine and draws away its evil."

sanskrit: gāvaḥ svargasya sopānaṃ gāvaḥ svarge 'pi pūjitāḥ gāvaḥ kāmadughā devyo nānyat kiṃ cit paraṃ smṛtam
english: "Cows are the stairway to heaven; cows are honored even in heaven. Cows are goddesses who yield every desire; nothing else is held to be higher."

sanskrit: ity etad goṣu me proktaṃ māhātmyaṃ pārthivarṣabha guṇaikadeśavacanaṃ śakyaṃ pārāyaṇaṃ na tu
english: "Thus has the glory of cows been proclaimed by me, O bull among kings—yet this is but the telling of a portion of their virtues; their full account cannot be exhausted."

sanskrit: niṣādā ūcuḥ darśanaṃ kathanaṃ caiva sahāsmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ mune satāṃ saptapadaṃ mitraṃ prasādaṃ naḥ kuru prabho
english: The Niṣādas said: "A meeting and a converse with us you have had, O sage; among the good, seven steps together make friendship. Show us your favor, O lord."

sanskrit: havīṃṣi sarvāṇi yathā hy upabhuṅkte hutāśanaḥ evaṃ tvam api dharmātman puruṣāgniḥ pratāpavān
english: "As the fire devours all oblations, so are you too, O righteous soul, a fire in the form of a man, blazing with power."

sanskrit: prasādayāmahe vidvan bhavantaṃ praṇatā vayam anugrahārtham asmākam iyaṃ gauḥ pratigṛhyatām
english: "We seek to win your favor, O learned one; bowed low are we. For the sake of grace toward us, let this cow be accepted."

sanskrit: cyavana uvāca kṛpaṇasya ca yac cakṣur muner āśīviṣasya ca naraṃ samūlaṃ dahati kakṣam agnir iva jvalan
english: Cyavana said: "The glance of one who is wretched, of a sage, and of a venomous serpent burns a man down to the root, as a blazing fire consumes the dry brushwood."

sanskrit: pratigṛhṇāmi vo dhenuṃ kaivartā muktakilbiṣāḥ divaṃ gacchata vai kṣipraṃ matsyair jāloddhṛtaiḥ saha
english: "I accept your milch-cow, O fishermen; freed from your sins are you. Go swiftly to heaven, together with the fish drawn up in your net."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tasya prasādāt te maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ niṣādās tena vākyena saha matsyair divaṃ yayuḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, by the grace of that great sage of purified soul, the Niṣādas, through that word, ascended to heaven together with the fish.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā nahuṣo vismitaḥ prekṣya dhīvarān ārohamāṇāṃs tridivaṃ matsyāṃś ca bharatarṣabha
english: Then King Nahuṣa was struck with wonder, beholding the fishermen, and the fish too, ascending to the threefold heaven, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tau gavijaś caiva cyavanaś ca bhṛgūdvahaḥ varābhyām anurūpābhyāṃ chandayām āsatur nṛpam
english: Then both the one born of a cow and Cyavana, the upholder of Bhṛgu's line, offered the king his choice of two fitting boons.

sanskrit: tato rājā mahāvīryo nahuṣaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ param ity abravīt prītas tadā bharatasattama
english: Then the mighty King Nahuṣa, lord of the earth, well pleased, said "It is excellent," O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tato jagrāha dharme sa sthitim indranibho nṛpaḥ tatheti coditaḥ prītas tāv ṛṣī pratyapūjayat
english: Then that king, equal to Indra, took up a firm standing in dharma; urged "So be it," he, well pleased, paid honor to those two sages in return.

sanskrit: samāptadīkṣaś cyavanas tato 'gacchat svam āśramam gavijaś ca mahātejāḥ svam āśramapadaṃ yayau
english: Then Cyavana, his consecration completed, went to his own hermitage, and the one born of a cow, of great splendor, returned to the site of his own hermitage.

sanskrit: niṣādāś ca divaṃ jagmus te ca matsyā janādhipa nahuṣo 'pi varaṃ labdhvā praviveśa puraṃ svakam
english: And the Niṣādas went to heaven, and so did the fish, O lord of men; and Nahuṣa too, having obtained his boon, entered his own city.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ tāta yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi darśane yādṛśaḥ snehaḥ saṃvāse ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: "This has been told to you, my son, that which you asked of me: what kind of affection arises in beholding one, and in dwelling together, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: mahābhāgyaṃ gavāṃ caiva tathā dharmaviniścayam kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathyatāṃ vīra kiṃ te hṛdi vivakṣitam
english: "And the great blessedness of cows, and likewise the determination of dharma. What more shall be told, O hero? What is it that you wish to ask in your heart?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca saṃśayo me mahāprājña sumahān sāgaropamaḥ tan me śṛṇu mahābāho śrutvā cākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "A doubt I have, O greatly wise one, vast as the ocean. Hear it from me, O mighty-armed one, and having heard, be pleased to explain it."

sanskrit: kautūhalaṃ me sumahaj jāmadagnyaṃ prati prabho rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: "Great is my curiosity, O lord, concerning the son of Jamadagni—Rāma, the foremost of the upholders of dharma. Be pleased to explain it to me."

sanskrit: katham eṣa samutpanno rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ kathaṃ brahmarṣivaṃśe ca kṣatradharmā vyajāyata
english: "How was this Rāma, whose valor is truth, brought forth? And how, in a line of brahmin-sages, was he born with the dharma of a kṣatriya?"

sanskrit: tad asya saṃbhavaṃ rājan nikhilenānukīrtaya kauśikāc ca kathaṃ vaṃśāt kṣatrād vai brāhmaṇo 'bhavat
english: "Recount his origin in full, O king; and how it was that from the Kauśika line, a kṣatriya line, there came to be a brahmin."

sanskrit: aho prabhāvaḥ sumahān āsīd vai sumahātmanoḥ rāmasya ca naravyāghra viśvāmitrasya caiva ha
english: "Ah, how very great was the power of those two great souls—of Rāma, O tiger among men, and of Viśvāmitra indeed."

sanskrit: kathaṃ putrān atikramya teṣāṃ naptṛṣv athābhavat eṣa doṣaḥ sutān hitvā tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: "How was it that, passing over their sons, this defect arose among their grandsons, leaving the sons aside? Be pleased to explain this to me."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam cyavanasya ca saṃvādaṃ kuśikasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the dialogue of Cyavana and of Kuśika, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etaṃ doṣaṃ purā dṛṣṭvā bhārgavaś cyavanas tadā āgāminaṃ mahābuddhiḥ svavaṃśe munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Foreseeing this defect of old as it was to come upon his own line, Cyavana the son of Bhṛgu, that bull among sages of great wisdom—

sanskrit: saṃcintya manasā sarvaṃ guṇadoṣabalābalam dagdhukāmaḥ kulaṃ sarvaṃ kuśikānāṃ tapodhanaḥ
english: —pondering in his mind the whole of it, its merits and defects, its strength and weakness, that ascetic resolved to burn down the entire family of the Kuśikas.

sanskrit: cyavanas tam anuprāpya kuśikaṃ vākyam abravīt vastum icchā samutpannā tvayā saha mamānagha
english: Cyavana, coming to that Kuśika, spoke these words: "A wish has arisen in me to dwell together with you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: kuśika uvāca bhagavan sahadharmo 'yaṃ paṇḍitair iha dhāryate pradānakāle kanyānām ucyate ca sadā budhaiḥ
english: Kuśika said: "Holy one, this is a duty to be shared in marriage, upheld here by the learned; it is spoken of by the wise always at the time of the giving of maidens."

sanskrit: yat tu tāvad atikrāntaṃ dharmadvāraṃ tapodhana tat kāryaṃ prakariṣyāmi tad anujñātum arhasi
english: "But as for that door of duty which has so far been passed by, O ascetic, that task I shall perform; be pleased to grant me leave for it."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca athāsanam upādāya cyavanasya mahāmuneḥ kuśiko bhāryayā sārdham ājagāma yato muniḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, taking up a seat for Cyavana the great sage, Kuśika, together with his wife, came to where the sage was.

sanskrit: pragṛhya rājā bhṛṅgāraṃ pādyam asmai nyavedayat kārayām āsa sarvāś ca kriyās tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Taking up a water-vessel, the king offered him water for his feet, and performed all the rites of welcome for that great soul.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā cyavanaṃ madhuparkaṃ yathāvidhi pratyagrāhayad avyagro mahātmā niyatavrataḥ
english: Then that king, the great-souled one, steadfast in his vows and unperturbed, had Cyavana receive the honey-and-curd offering according to rule.

sanskrit: satkṛtya sa tathā vipram idaṃ vacanam abravīt bhagavan paravantau svo brūhi kiṃ karavāvahe
english: Having thus honored the brahmin, he spoke these words: "Holy one, the two of us are at your command. Tell us, what shall we do?"

sanskrit: yadi rājyaṃ yadi dhanaṃ yadi gāḥ saṃśitavrata yajñadānāni ca tathā brūhi sarvaṃ dadāmi te
english: "Whether the kingdom, whether wealth, whether cows, O you of stern vows, and likewise sacrifices and gifts—say the word, and I shall give you all."

sanskrit: idaṃ gṛham idaṃ rājyam idaṃ dharmāsanaṃ ca te rājā tvam asi śādhy urvīṃ bhṛtyo 'haṃ paravāṃs tvayi
english: "This house, this kingdom, and this seat of dharma are yours. You are the king; govern the earth. I am your servant, dependent upon you."

sanskrit: evam ukte tato vākye cyavano bhārgavas tadā kuśikaṃ pratyuvācedaṃ mudā paramayā yutaḥ
english: When these words were spoken, then Cyavana the son of Bhṛgu, filled with the highest gladness, replied thus to Kuśika:

sanskrit: na rājyaṃ kāmaye rājan na dhanaṃ na ca yoṣitaḥ na ca gā na ca te deśān na yajñāñ śrūyatām idam
english: "I desire not the kingdom, O king, nor wealth, nor women, nor cows, nor your lands, nor sacrifices. Let this be heard:"

sanskrit: niyamaṃ kaṃ cid ārapsye yuvayor yadi rocate paricaryo 'smi yat tābhyāṃ yuvābhyām aviśaṅkayā
english: "I shall undertake a certain observance, if it pleases the two of you; and that you both should attend upon me without hesitation."

sanskrit: evam ukte tadā tena daṃpatī tau jaharṣatuḥ pratyabrūtāṃ ca tam ṛṣim evam astv iti bhārata
english: When this was spoken by him, the wedded pair rejoiced, and they answered that sage, "So be it," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: atha taṃ kuśiko hṛṣṭaḥ prāveśayad anuttamam gṛhoddeśaṃ tatas tatra darśanīyam adarśayat
english: Then Kuśika, delighted, led him into a most excellent quarter of the house, and there showed him a beautiful spot.

sanskrit: iyaṃ śayyā bhagavato yathākāmam ihoṣyatām prayatiṣyāvahe prītim āhartuṃ te tapodhana
english: "This is your couch, holy one; dwell here as you please. We two shall strive to bring you delight, O ascetic."

sanskrit: atha sūryo 'ticakrāma teṣāṃ saṃvadatāṃ tathā atharṣiś codayām āsa pānam annaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Now the sun passed onward while they were thus conversing, and the sage then called for drink and likewise for food.

sanskrit: tam apṛcchat tato rājā kuśikaḥ praṇatas tadā kim annajātam iṣṭaṃ te kim upasthāpayāmy aham
english: Then King Kuśika, bowing low, asked him: "What kind of food is desired by you? What shall I set before you?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sa parayā prītyā pratyuvāca janādhipam aupapattikam āhāraṃ prayacchasveti bhārata
english: Then he, with the utmost pleasure, replied to the lord of men: "Give me whatever food comes ready to hand," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad vacaḥ pūjayitvā tu tathety āha sa pārthivaḥ yathopapannaṃ cāhāraṃ tasmai prādāj janādhipaḥ
english: Honoring that word, the king said "So be it," and the lord of men gave him such food as was at hand.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān bhuktvā daṃpatī prāha dharmavit svaptum icchāmy ahaṃ nidrā bādhate mām iti prabho
english: Then that holy one, knower of dharma, having eaten, said to the wedded pair: "I wish to sleep; drowsiness oppresses me, O lord."

sanskrit: tataḥ śayyāgṛhaṃ prāpya bhagavān ṛṣisattamaḥ saṃviveśa narendras tu sapatnīkaḥ sthito 'bhavat
english: Then, reaching the sleeping-chamber, the holy one, best of sages, lay down; but the king, together with his wife, remained standing.

sanskrit: na prabodhyo 'smi saṃsupta ity uvācātha bhārgavaḥ saṃvāhitavyau pādau me jāgartavyaṃ ca vāṃ niśi
english: "I am not to be wakened once asleep," said the son of Bhṛgu then; "my feet are to be massaged, and you two must keep watch through the night."

sanskrit: aviśaṅkaś ca kuśikas tathety āha sa dharmavit na prabodhayatāṃ taṃ ca tau tadā rajanīkṣaye
english: And Kuśika, the knower of dharma, without hesitation said "So be it," and the two did not waken him even at the closing of the night.

sanskrit: yathādeśaṃ maharṣes tu śuśrūṣāparamau tadā babhūvatur mahārāja prayatāv atha daṃpatī
english: According to the great sage's command, the wedded pair, intent on his service and self-restrained, then remained so, O great king.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavān vipraḥ samādiśya narādhipam suṣvāpaikena pārśvena divasān ekaviṃśatim
english: Then that holy brahmin, having so instructed the king, slept upon a single side for twenty-one days.

sanskrit: sa tu rājā nirāhāraḥ sabhāryaḥ kurunandana paryupāsata taṃ hṛṣṭaś cyavanārādhane rataḥ
english: But that king, taking no food, together with his wife, O delight of the Kurus, attended upon him with gladness, devoted to the propitiation of Cyavana.

sanskrit: bhārgavas tu samuttasthau svayam eva tapodhanaḥ akiṃcid uktvā tu gṛhān niścakrāma mahātapāḥ
english: But the son of Bhṛgu, the ascetic, rose up of his own accord, and saying nothing at all, that great ascetic walked out of the house.

sanskrit: tam anvagacchatāṃ tau tu kṣudhitau śramakarśitau bhāryāpatī muniśreṣṭho na ca tāv avalokayat
english: The two of them followed after him, hungry and worn with toil, husband and wife; but the best of sages did not so much as look upon them.

sanskrit: tayos tu prekṣator eva bhārgavāṇāṃ kulodvahaḥ antarhito 'bhūd rājendra tato rājāpatat kṣitau
english: Even as the two of them looked on, the upholder of the line of the Bhārgavas vanished, O lord of kings; thereupon the king fell to the ground.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya saha devyā mahādyutiḥ punar anveṣaṇe yatnam akarot paramaṃ tadā
english: After resting a moment, that king of great splendor, together with his queen, then made the utmost effort to search for him once again.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca tasminn antarhite vipre rājā kim akarot tadā bhāryā cāsya mahābhāgā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "When that brahmin had vanished, what did the king do then, and his greatly blessed wife? Tell me that, O grandsire."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca adṛṣṭvā sa mahīpālas tam ṛṣiṃ saha bhāryayā pariśrānto nivavṛte vrīḍito naṣṭacetanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Not finding that sage, the protector of the earth, together with his wife, utterly spent, turned back, abashed and bereft of his senses.

sanskrit: sa praviśya purīṃ dīno nābhyabhāṣata kiṃ cana tad eva cintayām āsa cyavanasya viceṣṭitam
english: Entering the city, downcast, he spoke not a single word; he brooded only upon that conduct of Cyavana.

sanskrit: atha śūnyena manasā praviveśa gṛhaṃ nṛpaḥ dadarśa śayane tasmiñ śayānaṃ bhṛgunandanam
english: Then with a vacant mind the king entered his house, and he beheld, upon that very couch, the son of Bhṛgu lying asleep.

sanskrit: vismitau tau tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ tad āścaryaṃ vicintya ca darśanāt tasya ca muner viśrāntau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
english: The two of them, astonished, beholding him and pondering that marvel, became refreshed at the very sight of that sage.

sanskrit: yathāsthānaṃ tu tau sthitvā bhūyas taṃ saṃvavāhatuḥ athāpareṇa pārśvena suṣvāpa sa mahāmuniḥ
english: Taking their proper places, the two once more massaged him; and then that great sage slept upon his other side.

sanskrit: tenaiva ca sa kālena pratyabudhyata vīryavān na ca tau cakratuḥ kiṃ cid vikāraṃ bhayaśaṅkitau
english: And after that same span of time the mighty one awoke; yet the two, anxious with fear, showed no change of countenance at all.

sanskrit: pratibuddhas tu sa munis tau provāca viśāṃ pate tailābhyaṅgo dīyatāṃ me snāsye 'ham iti bhārata
english: Now the sage, having awakened, said to the two, O lord of peoples: "Let an anointing with oil be given me; I shall bathe," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatheti tau pratiśrutya kṣudhitau śramakarśitau śatapākena tailena mahārheṇopatasthatuḥ
english: Promising "So be it," the two, hungry and worn with toil, attended upon him with hundred-times-refined oil of great value.
